CACHE SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS
===================================

WHAT YOU THOUGHT WAS HAPPENING (Expected)
==========================================

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          USER                               │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │ Task("backend-dev", context)
                        │
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               CACHE SYSTEM (Layer 2-4)                      │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  1. Check cache_manager.get(query)                  │   │
│  │  2. If HIT → return cached (95% of time)           │   │
│  │  3. If MISS → continue to API                       │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │ Only on cache MISS (5% of time)
                        │
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    CLAUDE API                               │
│          (Layer 1: Built-in Prompt Cache)                   │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │ Response
                        │
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Cache stores response via cache_manager.set()             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Expected Savings: 95% (5% API calls, 95% cache hits)
Expected Cost: $3-25/month


WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING (Reality)
=====================================

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          USER                               │
└───────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            │ Task("backend-dev", context)
                            │
                            ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              CLAUDE CODE TASK TOOL                          │
│  • Creates NEW session ID every time                        │
│  • Fresh conversation context                               │
│  • Isolated execution environment                           │
│  • NO cache integration                                     │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │ EVERY TIME (100%)
                        │
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    CLAUDE API                               │
│          (Layer 1: Built-in Prompt Cache)                   │
│  • Only 5-10% reuse within single session                   │
│  • New session = no cache benefit                           │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │ Response
                        │
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    USER GETS RESULT                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         cache_manager.py (ORPHANED - NEVER CALLED)          │
│  • Sitting idle in .claude/cache/                           │
│  • Has hot/cold/semantic layers ready                       │
│  • Only used by manual test scripts                         │
│  • Zero integration with Task tool                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Actual Savings: 5-10% (Claude's built-in only)
Actual Cost: $400-425/month


WHY THE GAP EXISTS
==================

cache_manager.py is designed as:

    from cache_manager import CacheManager

    cache = CacheManager()
    result = cache.get(query)  # Requires explicit call

    if result:
        return result
    else:
        api_response = call_claude_api(query)
        cache.set(query, api_response)
        return api_response

This works when YOU control the API call.

Task tool workflow:

    Task("backend-dev", context)
      → Claude Code internal routing
      → New Claude API session
      → Agent executes
      → Response

    No place to insert cache.get() or cache.set()

Task tool is a BLACK BOX from your perspective.


SOLUTION OPTIONS
================

OPTION 1: ACCEPT REALITY (DONE)
--------------------------------

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  USER → Task Tool → Claude API (5-10% cache) → Response    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Documentation now reflects this reality.


OPTION 2: MCP SERVER INTEGRATION (2-3 hours)
---------------------------------------------

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          USER                               │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │ Task("backend-dev", context)
                        │
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              CLAUDE CODE TASK TOOL                          │
│  • Loads MCP servers                                        │
│  • Agent sees cache.get() and cache.set() tools             │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │ Agent's code execution
                        │
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    AGENT LOGIC                              │
│                                                             │
│  if needs_answer:                                           │
│      cached = cache.get(query)  ← MCP TOOL CALL            │
│      if cached:                                             │
│          return cached                                      │
│      else:                                                  │
│          answer = think_and_respond()                       │
│          cache.set(query, answer)  ← MCP TOOL CALL         │
│          return answer                                      │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │ MCP protocol
                        │
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            CACHE MCP SERVER                                 │
│  • Receives cache.get/set requests                          │
│  • Calls cache_manager.py                                   │
│  • Returns results to agent                                 │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         cache_manager.py (NOW USED!)                        │
│  • Hot/cold/semantic cache layers                           │
│  • Returns cached responses                                 │
│  • Stores new responses                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Expected Savings: 60-80% (agents must remember to cache)
Expected Cost: $90-180/month


OPTION 3: PROXY WRAPPER (8-10 hours, NOT RECOMMENDED)
------------------------------------------------------

Create custom wrapper:

    def cached_task(agent, context):
        key = hash(f"{agent}:{context}")
        cached = cache.get(key)
        if cached:
            return cached
        result = Task(agent, context)
        cache.set(key, result)
        return result

Problems:
- Can't modify Claude Code Task tool
- User must remember to use cached_task() instead of Task()
- Context hashing is tricky
- Not integrated with UI
- High maintenance burden


THE REAL ARCHITECTURAL ISSUE
=============================

cache_manager.py:         Library (requires explicit calls)
Task tool:                Black box (you can't inject cache calls)
Result:                   No integration point

Claude Code is designed for:
  • Agent delegation
  • Tool usage (Read, Write, Bash, etc.)
  • MCP server integration

NOT designed for:
  • Custom middleware layers
  • API call interception
  • Session persistence across Task calls


WHY MCP IS THE RIGHT ANSWER
============================

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is:
  • Built into Claude Code
  • Exposes tools to agents
  • Agents can call tools explicitly
  • Supported integration method

Implementation:

1. Create cache-mcp-server.py:
   - Exposes cache.get(query)
   - Exposes cache.set(query, response)
   - Calls cache_manager.py internally

2. Add to mcp.json:
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "cache": {
         "command": "python",
         "args": [".claude/cache/cache-mcp-server.py"]
       }
     }
   }

3. Update agent prompts:
   "Before answering repeated questions, check cache.get(query)"

4. Agent workflow becomes:
   Agent: I should check cache first
   Agent: [calls cache.get("How to implement JWT?")]
   MCP: Returns cached response
   Agent: Uses cached answer


LIMITATIONS OF MCP APPROACH
============================

NOT automatic:
  • Agents must remember to cache
  • Requires agent logic changes
  • Won't work for first-time questions

Partial savings:
  • Only works when agent uses cache tools
  • Not all queries will be cached
  • Expected 60-80% (not 95%)

Maintenance:
  • Agent prompts must mention caching
  • MCP server must be maintained
  • Additional complexity


BOTTOM LINE
===========

Current Architecture:
  Task tool → Claude API (isolated sessions)
  cache_manager.py → Never called
  Result: 5-10% savings

Option 1 (Honest docs):
  Accept 5-10% savings
  Know real costs
  No work needed

Option 2 (MCP integration):
  Expose cache as MCP server
  Agents call cache explicitly
  60-80% savings (not automatic)
  2-3 hours work

Recommended:
  Option 1 unless costs are prohibitive
  Then consider Option 2
  Never do Option 3
